answer.rationale: The tempting move is switch_primary_vendor: memory_c2 says exactly that cut unit cost sharply, and the low-cost quote meets the 18% mandate on its own. But c2 is the single most load-bearing memory for the highest-risk action, and what it actually records is cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy \u nothing about on-time delivery under load, yield, or performance during a demand peak. Last year's switch may also have happened with slack in the line; today there is none (94% of committed volume, no buffer, 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew). A vendor change that fails even briefly converts a cost win into missed customer commitments, which is a worse outcome than missing part of the spend target. So I verify c2 to see whether the archived record covers delivery performance and what the starting conditions were, and c4 to check whether the benchmark-driven renegotiation actually moved price materially or only payment terms \u that determines whether negotiation can plausibly approach 18%. Intended action: negotiate_terms with the incumbent, using the low-cost quote as documented leverage, with c6 suggesting a multi-year structure can unlock volume pricing without narrowing service scope. This is the reversible move: it protects the c1 integration stability and delivery continuity while attacking cost, and it keeps switching available next cycle. Scale is deliberately guarded \u a term/price renegotiation plus, at most, a small qualification volume with the low-cost vendor rather than a primary-supply migration \u because the cost evidence for switching is real but incomplete on exactly the dimension (delivery risk) that the objective forbids increasing. add_second_source (c3) is attractive on resilience but does not address the mandate this cycle; defer_decision (c5) applied to a non-critical renewal and is unsafe here because this contract does not auto-renew. If verification shows c4's renegotiation was terms-only and c2's switch held up on delivery through a comparable peak, I would escalate toward a staged vendor transition next cycle rather than now. I am not treating the inherited memories as settled outcomes \u each records a success without its failure counterfactual, and the current constraint stack is not the one they were learned under.
